Marisol asked whether to run a 16-miler on Wednesday. The draft gives a clear, honest no: a long run three or four days before the race won't add fitness by Sunday and will leave her legs flat at the start. That's the most important call this week, and it's correct.

The race-week plan keeps her usual pattern. Monday and Friday are off, Wednesday is a short marathon-pace session, and Sunday is the race. The pre-race running comes to about 15 miles after a 34-mile week, which is a sensible taper with no jump in volume or long run. The 8:35/mi marathon pace works out to about 3:45, so it matches her goal. Starting slower for the first 2 miles is good pacing advice. Every day can be run as written.

Nothing here breaks a safety rule. She says nothing hurts, so there are no injury signs that need a referral. Heavy, dead legs are normal during a taper, not the exhaustion or poor sleep that would call for backing off further. The week already eases off.

I took off one point because, from what's visible, the draft doesn't directly speak to her nerves or her worry about losing fitness. It could have told her plainly that flat legs are normal in a taper and her fitness is already built. The opening message is cut off, though, so it may have done that.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 53, 40, 42, 46 mi
This week: 34 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs heavy and flat. Nothing hurts, they just feel dead."
Feeling: "Nervous. I feel like I'm losing fitness."
Asks: "Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Race week. …
Answers: No, do not add a 16-miler on Wednesday. A long run three or four days out will not build any fitness that shows up by Sunday, but it will absolutely leave your legs flat on the start line.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to start the taper properly.
Tue: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, then 4 x 20 sec strides. Keeps the legs turning…
Wed: quality, 5 mi, with 3 x 1 mi at marathon pace (8:35/mi), 90 sec jog between. Short…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, very relaxed, heart rate under 140. Flush the legs after Wednesday.
Fri: rest. Sleep, hydrate, add a little extra carbohydrate at meals.
Sat: easy, 2 mi, shakeout pace, plus 4 x 20 sec strides. Wakes the system up without…
Sun: race, Wexley Lakes Marathon, 26.2 mi. First 2 mi at 8:45 to 8:50, settle to 8:35…
